newsitem.title: USA: LaserSight hopes to expand clinical trials.
newsitem.headline: LaserSight hopes to expand clinical trials.

text.p: LaserSight Inc said Wednesday that it anticipates asking in early 1997 for U.S. Food and Drug Administration permission to move to human trials for its laser scanning technology to correct nearsightedness.

LaserSight won a patent in May, has ISO 9002 certification and expects a European CE Mark regulatory designation in the fourth quarter which would allow increased marketing in Europe, the company said in its third quarter statement.
In addition, it said new credit policies on receivables, announced earlier, helped third quarter payment terms.
As reported earlier, LaserSight posted a third quarter loss of $0.28 a share versus net income of $0.11 a year ago.
Revenues declined to $4.5 million from $6.8 million due to new return policies, lower prices on units sold, fewer units shipped and decreased consulting services activities, it said.
It said its managed care subsidiary has expanded existing contracts with Kaiser Permanente and Healthplan Southeast.
LaserSight has four operating subsidiaries engaged in ophthalmic laser manufacturing, third-party managed vision care, vision care practice management and health and vision care consulting.
